title: [v0.4.29] Release: Linux, WSL2 and macOS
author: mcpdev80
body:
**Windows scope:** v0.4 supports the developer path through real WSL2 with Linux baha. A native Windows executable/host adapter and Windows containers are outside this release; build-only Windows evidence does not establish native runtime support.

Parent: #427 · Implementation umbrella: #818 · Related: #817, #174 · Depends on v0.4.28 #875

## Goal and authoritative scope

Deliver real Linux, WSL2 and macOS developer workflows while preserving the portable semantics set in v0.4.25 #872. Host mechanisms belong behind host/runtime adapters. Implementation defects may be fixed with regression evidence; semantic changes require explicit review before #174/v0.4.31 freezes the contract.

This consolidated scope replaces the earlier conflicting v0.4.25 assignment, two-PR wording and macOS Local+Remote acceptance in this issue.

| Platform/use case | v0.4.29 obligation |
| --- | --- |
| Native Linux Docker and rootless Podman | Existing behavior, security and real acceptance preserved |
| Genuine WSL2 | Existing #821 Dev Local **and Dev Remote** scope remains required; Windows-hosted builds are not WSL2 proof |
| macOS darwin/arm64 | Full Dev Local with **both Docker Desktop and Podman Machine**, real runtime evidence and independent walkthrough |
| macOS darwin/amd64 | Artifacts, native build/unit/conformance where runners are available; runtime support only with its own real evidence |
| macOS Dev Remote and automatic Keychain trust | Explicitly deferred to #886; not advertised as delivered by v0.4.29 |
| Developer ID signing/notarization | Explicitly deferred to #885 |
| Native Windows runtime/Windows containers; Colima/OrbStack/Rancher Desktop | No support claim without separately scoped real evidence |

The macOS deferrals are an explicit delivery decision, not an unnoticed reduction of acceptance. Host trust in v0.4.29 is manual: export, documented user action and read-only verified status. Runtime/workload TLS validation remains required.

## Work ownership and sequence

**Session 1:** #819 host seam/contract review, #820 Linux reference and #821 Windows/WSL2. Own shared host interfaces and Linux/WSL2 adapters; publish the boundary before downstream work.

**Session 2:** #822 Darwin/distribution/Docker Desktop, #883 Podman Machine executor, #823 conformance/support evidence and #884 real Mac runner. Own Darwin/platform qualification; coordinate shared interfaces with Session 1. #817 audits the result.

Sequence: #882 Darwin compilation prerequisite → #819 D1/D2 review → #820 Linux reference → #822 Darwin/Docker Desktop and #883 Podman Machine → #823/#884 qualification → #817 audit.

Use **one shared release PR** against `release/v0.4.29`, separate local checkouts and scoped commits on the same integration branch. Check remote HEAD before changes/pushes, preserve other commits, coordinate shared files, no force-push. #882 is the explicit separate prerequisite PR targeting `develop`; integrate its exact result into the release candidate. Tests first; full pre-release/promotion/tag/publication require their own authorization.

## Reviewed decisions

### D1 — observed engine isolation

`vm-isolated` is a separately reviewed engine classification, not proof of security equivalence to rootless. Preserve both observed privilege and execution-location facts: a rootless engine can also run in a VM.

Require positive evidence linking the selected endpoint to the selected running VM/machine, its owner and access boundary. A context name, executable, socket path, Darwin host or reported rootful status alone is insufficient. Endpoint/machine mismatch or unknown provenance must produce a typed diagnosis, not fallback to a privileged host daemon.

Validate VM-side filesystem/resource ownership and host bind-mount/file-sharing permissions. VM root must not grant unreviewed access to foreign host paths or engine sockets. Preserve existing workload policy, user choice and explicit rootful-host opt-in. Exact vendor discovery mechanisms stay provider-internal; review public semantic changes before dependent implementation.

Owned by #819; update the pinned Engine selection semantics only after explicit contract review.

### D2 — effective runtime capacity

Capacity evidence must identify the selected engine/VM, source, timestamp, applicable limits and quality (measured / estimated / unknown). Physical-host RAM is not a substitute for effective runtime capacity.

`MemTotal` is capacity, not available memory; `MemFree` alone is not Linux `MemAvailable`. `VM MemTotal - sum(docker stats)` is only a partial estimate: it omits VM OS/daemon/non-container use and depends on cache accounting. It MUST NOT, by itself, establish SAFE or a guaranteed available budget.

Prefer non-mutating observations of runtime-visible available memory/pressure and effective limits where supported. If only partial estimates exist, report their limits and uncertainty; do not turn missing evidence into a safe admission. Preserve the existing typed admission/remediation model. Any policy for an explicit user decision under uncertainty needs contract review; no implicit admission bypass and no mutation during plan/preflight.

Linux retains `/proc/meminfo`/PSI evidence and cross-checks applicable engine/VM/cgroup limits; the constraining effective budget governs. Darwin consumes selected VM evidence. Host presentation must consume the same result, not independently infer capacity. Owned by #819/#820.

### D3 — one Podman realization

#883 executes existing Quadlet/systemd realization inside the selected Podman Machine Linux VM through a narrow provider-internal executor. No second Compose/kube-play implementation and no generic remote-exec/MCP surface. Preserve local Linux behavior and VM-side ownership.

### D4 — four distinct evidence lanes

#823 records four separate lanes: Darwin cross-build, native Darwin conformance, Linux/arm64 container stack, and real macOS runtime. Cross-build/native tests cannot replace a container lifecycle proof. Hosted Apple-Silicon constraints motivate the dedicated trusted-trigger self-hosted Mac in #884. Record actual runner/engine/OS versions and exact sources.

### D5 — distribution and trust

#882 restores Darwin compilation. #822 adds darwin/arm64 and amd64 packaging, checksums, provenance/attestation subjects, installer and self-update selection. Ad-hoc signing is not Developer ID identity or notarization; verify actual artifacts per architecture. Qualify installation/update on a clean Mac. Observe and document quarantine/Gatekeeper behavior of installer and browser paths rather than promise universal bypass. #885 owns later signing/notarization.

## Developer journey and acceptance

- [ ] #882 Darwin build/vet passes for both architectures; Linux secret/terminal semantics preserved.
- [ ] D1/D2 reviewed, recorded in the pinned spec and covered by negative conformance tests before consumers depend on them.
- [ ] Linux Docker/rootless Podman regression acceptance passes.
- [ ] Genuine WSL2 #821 Dev Local/Remote, trust separation, effective capacity, cleanup and independent walkthrough pass.
- [ ] Candidate Darwin packages install/update with checksum/provenance validation; published-artifact checks follow authorized release publication.
- [ ] Both macOS arm64 engines pass install/init/plan/up/status/doctor/logs/sql/cache/owned destroy on one exact matrix via #884.
- [ ] Negative cases: stopped/missing VM, endpoint/machine mismatch, unknown/insufficient capacity, unshared or foreign path, denied permissions, broken trust and safe cleanup.
- [ ] Repository/bind-mount paths are verified in the VM before mutation; ownership and socket policy remain enforced.
- [ ] Browser and curl reach canonical development HTTPS routes, including IPv4/IPv6 behavior and the documented manual trust step.
- [ ] Linux/arm64 container stack, Darwin-native adapter/PTY/filesystem/ephemeral-secret tests and real Mac journeys have distinct receipts.
- [ ] Independent macOS Dev Local and WSL2 walkthroughs succeed from public EN/DE docs; avoidable prompts/friction recorded.
- [ ] #805 support matrix and Doctor report per-combination evidence honestly; amd64/alternative engines are not promoted from arm64 proof.
- [ ] #817 architecture audit passes; #885/#886 deferrals remain explicit in documentation and release scope.

Support transitions require exact-source evidence: macOS arm64 TESTED after real journeys, SUPPORTED only after required candidate qualification and independent walkthrough. No platform claim follows merely from build success.
